statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail stands at 12 of 100 in the low band, thirteen points below the 25 block threshold, while stress is extreme at 86 and confidence high at 88.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The named danger window spans the 12:30 UTC August consumer price report, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 UTC preliminary Michigan release, where the conditional path peaks at WATCH without reaching the block threshold.
headline: NQ trades 29,085.75, down 0.17%, after extending the overnight low to 29,042.00 and recovering about 44 points off it, which holds tail at 12, while a 4.944% ten-year, Brent near $108 and a September rate increase priced close to a coin flip keep stress extreme at 86 into the August consumer price report.
body:
The new evidence this hour is the first genuine extension of the overnight range, immediately followed by a retracement. NQ trades 29,085.75, down 49.50 points or 0.17%, against an overnight band of 29,042.00 to 29,171.50. An hour ago the low stood at 29,061.75 and had been extended by less than a point since the 22:00 UTC reopen. It has now been pushed about 20 points lower, and price has recovered roughly 44 points from it. A second independent quote source reports 29,080.25 with a 29,040.50 low, so both the extension and the recovery are confirmed on two feeds.

That sequence is what keeps tail at 12 rather than lifting it. Tail measures a persistent no-retracement price path, not direction and not the act of making a new low. A low that is probed and then bought back by a third of the band's width is the signature of a market still finding two-way interest at its extremes. The amplifiers that would matter are absent: there is no repeated extension after failed retracements, no shallow-pullback sequence, and no acceptance below the old low. The band is now about 130 points wide, roughly 0.45%, which remains a contained overnight range. The deterministic mapping therefore returns EA_ON for both instruments.

The backdrop is why stress stays extreme at 86. The ten-year Treasury yield closed at 4.944%, up 10.7 basis points on the session with an intraday high of 4.952%, its highest since 2023, and the thirty-year sits at 5.35%. The two-year is 4.581%. Brent trades near $107.90 and WTI near $102.41, with the Strait of Hormuz supply premium intact. The VIX closed at 17.84, up from 16.46. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 29,103.51, down 1.08%, a fourth consecutive losing session. Overnight the rates complex is marginally calmer, with the ten-year and two-year each about a basis point lower, which is consistent with the observed stabilisation in futures rather than at odds with it.

The scheduled agenda dominates the forward window. August consumer prices are released at 12:30 UTC, with consensus at 0.4% month over month and 3.4% year over year for the headline, and 0.2% and 2.4% for core. Surveyed core estimates cluster between 0.16% and 0.24%, so dispersion is unusually narrow and the surprise channel sits largely in the rounding. This is the last inflation reading before the 16 September Federal Reserve decision, where consensus has shifted to a 25 basis point increase to 4.00% and market-implied odds have been quoted in the low-to-high sixties after Thursday's producer price report. Conditional tail peaks at 23 in the 12:00 UTC slot and 22 across the cash open, inside the watch band, because an inflation surprise more reliably produces two-way repricing than the sustained no-retracement leg the score describes.

The shared Finviz cross-asset context was not used as evidence in this assessment. Its collection status is partial and its timestamp is roughly three hours old, beyond the freshness limit the contract sets for supporting use, so the assessment rests entirely on independently fetched primary sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 04:00 UTC on 10 September to 03:00 UTC on 11 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 10 and holds a 9 to 11 band through the U.S. overnight, the Asian session and the European morning, with the dominant mode recorded as mixed throughout. The regime change sits in the middle of the U.S. session: tail 14 at 11:00 UTC as the mode turned trend-down on the pre-release grind, 20 at 12:00 UTC when the August producer price report printed and the mode became event/whipsaw, and the window peak of 24 at 13:00 UTC across the cash open, the only slot at the top of the watch band. Tail then decayed as price discovery stayed orderly, easing to 17 by 14:00 UTC and holding 14 to 19 through the afternoon, with event/whipsaw recorded again at 19:00 and 20:00 UTC around the cash close. From the 22:00 UTC futures reopen the series settles back into the overnight regime, 15 then 14, 13, 12, 11 and 12, with the mode mixed in every one of those slots. Stress never left the extreme band, ranging from 80 at the start of the window to a peak of 87, and confidence held between 84 and 89 throughout. Two slots carried a WATCH mapping, at 12:00 and 13:00 UTC; the other twenty-two mapped to EA_ON.
outlookSummary: The forward window opens with about six hours of observed post-reopen trade on 11 September, covers the full U.S. session, and then ends inside the CME weekend closure that begins at 21:00 UTC. Conditional tail starts at 12, holds 12 through the late Asian hours and dips to an 11 floor in the thinnest pre-European hour, where no U.S. macro is scheduled. From the European cash open it rebuilds gradually, 12 through 14, reaching 16 in the final full hour before the release as quoted depth conditionally thins. The window peak is 23 in the 12:00 UTC slot containing the August consumer price report, which stays inside the watch band and below the 25 block threshold, and 22 in the 13:00 UTC slot spanning the cash open, where a post-event move is most often confirmed or rejected. The 14:00 UTC slot carrying the preliminary Michigan release eases to 19 on the assumption that price discovery is orderly, and the afternoon decays from 17 to 14 before ticking back to 15 and 18 into the weekly close, where rebalancing flow and pre-decision positioning concentrate. From 21:00 UTC the futures market is halted for the weekend: tail drops to 6 and then 5, and stress falls from the extreme band to 64 and then 61, because a closed market cannot produce the intraday drawdown the stress score describes, while weekend gap exposure into the Sunday reopen remains. Confidence declines gently from 88 to 81 across the closure, reflecting the age of the underlying evidence rather than any defect in it. Only the 12:00 and 13:00 UTC slots map to WATCH; the other twenty-two map to EA_ON.
